summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of ischemic systolic heart failure, coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia, was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure triggered by non-compliance with his furosemide for two weeks. He presented with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and increased pedal edema. In the hospital, he was treated with intravenous furosemide, leading to improved symptoms and a weight reduction to 137.8 kg. An echocardiogram showed improved ejection fraction of 35–40%. He had episodes of supraventricular tachycardia, prompting an increase in metoprolol and outpatient Holter monitoring. His lisinopril was held due to elevated creatinine, and he was transitioned from atorvastatin to simvastatin for financial reasons. GERD symptoms improved with omeprazole. He was discharged home on optimized medical therapy, compression stockings, and instructions for weight monitoring and follow-up.
